facts.statement: Wrote travel, essays, poetry and fiction; Treasure Island 1883 and Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde 1886.
Settled at Vailima in Samoa in his later years.

interpretation.note: Interpretation of the documented life and works; no claim of personal acquaintance from shared themes.

appraisal.note: AETERNUS editorial judgement; not presented as a historical quotation.

en.tagline: The traveller’s eye and the storyteller’s moral imagination.
en.intro: Stevenson’s adventures begin in the movement of a distinctive voice: observant, companionable and alert to danger. The road, the sea and the divided self gave him different ways of testing a story.
en.orientation: The famous romances belong beside the essays, journeys and Pacific writings. Together they reveal a writer whose geographical range was matched by a range of forms.
origin: Born in Edinburgh into a family associated with lighthouse engineering, he turned from the expected professional path towards literature.
career: European journeys and transatlantic travel preceded the Pacific years. At Vailima in Samoa he wrote from within a society exposed to competing foreign ambitions.
literature: Treasure Island and Jekyll and Hyde achieved different kinds of narrative concentration. The travel books preserve another Stevenson: a writer attentive to the pace, discomfort and encounters of a journey.
en.legacy: His work keeps adventure intellectually alive. A clear surface can carry questions about allegiance, identity and the price of a chosen life.
en.bridge: The editions follow the individual book back into the wider art of a writer whose journeys were also experiments in prose.
